423: class Hud:
424:     """Click-through transparent overlay drawn straight onto the game.
425: 
426:     Two rules, both forced by the measurement physics:
427: 
428:     1. NEVER draw between 0.92R and 1.42R. That band is what the occupancy
429:        scan reads; ink there would be measured as a knife.
430:     2. Ink inside the capture box is BLUE-dominant (B > R + 25) so that even
431:        if it is photographed, the sky mask files it as background, not as an
432:        obstacle.
433: 
434:     Status text and the live dot sit OUTSIDE the capture rectangle, where they
435:     cannot be photographed at all.
436:     """
437: 
438:     KEY = "#ff00ff"       # magenta = transparent key colour
439:     INK = "#00d8ff"       # cyan-blue: reads as 'sky' to the mask
440:     GO = "#31ff6b"
441:     BAD = "#ff3b3b"
442: 
443:     def __init__(self, sw: int, sh: int, enabled: bool = True,
444:                  use_wda: bool = True):
445:         self.ok = False
446:         self.closed = False
447:         if not enabled:
448:             self.closed = True
449:             return
450:         try:
451:             import tkinter as tk
452:             self.root = tk.Tk()
453:             self.root.overrideredirect(True)
454:             self.root.geometry(f"{sw}x{sh}+0+0")
455:             self.root.attributes("-topmost", True)
456:             self.root.attributes("-transparentcolor", self.KEY)
457:             self.canvas = tk.Canvas(self.root, width=sw, height=sh,
458:                                     bg=self.KEY, highlightthickness=0, bd=0)
459:             self.canvas.pack()
460:             self.root.update_idletasks()
461: 
462:             hwnd = ctypes.windll.user32.GetParent(self.root.winfo_id())
463:             if not hwnd:
464:                 hwnd = self.root.winfo_id()
465:             GWL_EXSTYLE = -20
466:             ex = ctypes.windll.user32.GetWindowLongW(hwnd, GWL_EXSTYLE)
467:             ctypes.windll.user32.SetWindowLongW(
468:                 hwnd, GWL_EXSTYLE, ex | 0x80000 | 0x20 | 0x08000000)
469:                 # LAYERED | TRANSPARENT | NOACTIVATE : clicks pass through and
470:                 # it never steals focus from the game.
471:             try:
472:                 if use_wda:
473:                     ok = ctypes.windll.user32.SetWindowDisplayAffinity(hwnd, 0x11)
474:                     print("[hud] display affinity WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE: "
475:                           f"{'accepted' if ok else 'REFUSED'}")
476:                 else:
477:                     print("[hud] display affinity disabled "
478:                           "(--no-wda): the overlay WILL be captured")
479:             except Exception as exc:                           # noqa: BLE001
480:                 print(f"[hud] display affinity failed ({exc})")
481:             self.ok = True
482:             print("[hud] overlay active (click-through, lines over the game)")
483:         except Exception as exc:                               # noqa: BLE001
484:             print(f"[hud] unavailable ({exc}) -- no overlay")
485: 
486:     def verify(self, sct, mon: dict) -> bool:
487:         """Prove the key colour is actually transparent before trusting it.
488: 
489:         If -transparentcolor silently fails, this window becomes an opaque
490:         magenta sheet covering the entire game -- the worst possible outcome.
491:         Photograph a corner we never draw in and check it is not magenta.
492:         """
493:         if not self.ok or self.closed:
494:             return True
495:         try:
496:             self.root.update()
497:             time.sleep(0.10)
498:             reg = {"left": mon["left"] + 4, "top": mon["top"] + 4,
499:                    "width": 16, "height": 16}
500:             raw = sct.grab(reg)
501:             px = np.frombuffer(raw.bgra, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(-1, 4)[:, :3]
502:             b = float(px[:, 0].mean())
503:             g = float(px[:, 1].mean())
504:             r = float(px[:, 2].mean())
505:             if b > 200 and r > 200 and g < 80:
506:                 print("[hud] WARNING: transparency FAILED -- the overlay is an")
507:                 print("      opaque magenta sheet. Disabling it so you can still")
508:                 print("      see the game. Tell me and I will fix the mechanism.")
509:                 self.close()
510:                 return False
511:             print(f"[hud] transparency verified (corner rgb "
512:                   f"{r:.0f},{g:.0f},{b:.0f})")
513:             return True
514:         except Exception as exc:                               # noqa: BLE001
515:             print(f"[hud] verify skipped ({exc})")
516:             return True
517: 
518:     def draw(self, cx: float, cy: float, r: float, bbox: dict, d: dict) -> None:
519:         if not self.ok or self.closed:
520:             return
521:         c = self.canvas
522:         ink = self.INK
523:         try:
524:             c.delete("all")
525:             x0, y0 = bbox["left"], bbox["top"]
526:             x1, y1 = x0 + bbox["width"], y0 + bbox["height"]
527: 
528:             c.create_rectangle(x0, y0, x1, y1, outline=ink, width=2)
529:             c.create_oval(cx - r, cy - r, cx + r, cy + r, outline=ink, width=2)
530: 
531:             for a, _w in d["obs"]:
532:                 pa = math.radians(a)
533:                 c.create_line(cx + r * 1.44 * math.cos(pa),
534:                               cy + r * 1.44 * math.sin(pa),
535:                               cx + r * 1.50 * math.cos(pa),
536:                               cy + r * 1.50 * math.sin(pa), fill=ink, width=2)
537:             for a, w in d["gaps"]:
538:                 pa = math.radians(a)
539:                 c.create_text(cx + r * 1.54 * math.cos(pa),
540:                               cy + r * 1.54 * math.sin(pa),
541:                               text=f"{w:.0f}", fill=ink,
542:                               font=("Consolas", 9, "bold"))
543:             if d["spokes"]:
544:                 for kk in range(60):
545:                     pa = math.radians(kk * 6.0 - 90.0)
546:                     c.create_line(cx + r * 1.44 * math.cos(pa),
547:                                   cy + r * 1.44 * math.sin(pa),
548:                                   cx + r * 1.55 * math.cos(pa),
549:                                   cy + r * 1.55 * math.sin(pa), fill=ink)
550:                     c.create_text(cx + r * 1.62 * math.cos(pa),
551:                                   cy + r * 1.62 * math.sin(pa),
552:                                   text=f"L{kk + 1}", fill=ink,
553:                                   font=("Consolas", 7))
554: 
555:             if d["alive"]:
556:                 dot_y = y0 - 30 if y0 > 60 else y1 + 22
557:                 c.create_oval(x0 + 4, dot_y - 5, x0 + 14, dot_y + 5,
558:                               fill=self.GO, outline="")
559:                 c.create_text(x0 + 20, dot_y, anchor="w",
560:                               text=f"LIVE {d['fps']:.1f}fps  w {d['omega']:.0f}d/s"
561:                                    f"  conf {d['conf']:.2f}  gap {d['gap']:.0f}",
562:                               fill=self.GO, font=("Consolas", 10, "bold"))
563:                 c.create_text(x0 + 4, dot_y + 16, anchor="w",
564:                               text=f"capturing {bbox['width']}x{bbox['height']}"
565:                                    f"  (this box)",
566:                               fill="#c8c8c8", font=("Consolas", 9))
567:             self.root.update()
568:         except Exception:                                       # noqa: BLE001
569:             pass
570: 
571:     def close(self) -> None:
572:         if self.ok and not self.closed:
573:             self.closed = True
574:             try:
575:                 self.root.destroy()
576:             except Exception:                                   # noqa: BLE001
577:                 pass
578: 
579: 
580: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
581: # Preview window
582: # --------------------------------------------------------------------------- #
583: class Preview:
584:     """Tkinter preview.
585: 
586:     WHY NOT cv2.imshow: the OpenCV wheel on this machine is built without
587:     HighGUI, so imshow() raises 'The function is not implemented'. Tk + PIL is
588:     already installed and works. The window is refreshed at ~25 Hz and is
589:     deliberately independent of the capture rate -- drawing must never throttle
590:     measurement.
591:     """
592: 
593:     def __init__(self, scale: float = 0.6, pos=None, enabled: bool = True):
594:         self.ok = False
595:         self.key = None
596:         self.scale = scale
597:         self.pos = pos
598:         self.closed = False
599:         self.item = None
600:         if not enabled:
601:             self.closed = True
602:             return
603:         try:
604:             import tkinter as tk
605:             from PIL import Image, ImageTk
606:             self.tk, self.Image, self.ImageTk = tk, Image, ImageTk
607: 
608:             self.root = tk.Tk()
609:             self.root.title("knife-rush telemetry    [q]uit [c]alib [d]ump [r]eset [+/-]T [p]review")
610:             self.canvas = tk.Canvas(self.root, width=360, height=270,
611:                                     highlightthickness=0, bg="black")
612:             self.canvas.pack()
613:             self.root.bind("<Key>", self._on_key)
614:             self.root.protocol("WM_DELETE_WINDOW", self.close)
615:             self.ok = True
616:         except Exception as exc:                                  # noqa: BLE001
617:             print(f"[preview] unavailable ({exc}) -- running headless")
618: 
619:     def _on_key(self, event) -> None:
620:         self.key = event.keysym
621: 
622:     def show(self, vis):
623:         if not self.ok or self.closed:
624:             return None
625:         h, w = vis.shape[:2]
626:         s = self.scale
627:         small = cv2.resize(vis, (max(1, int(w * s)), max(1, int(h * s))),
628:                            interpolation=cv2.INTER_NEAREST)
629:         rgb = cv2.cvtColor(small, cv2.COLOR_BGR2RGB)
630:         photo = self.ImageTk.PhotoImage(self.Image.fromarray(rgb))
631:         if self.item is None:
632:             self.item = self.canvas.create_image(0, 0, anchor="nw", image=photo)
633:             self.canvas.config(width=rgb.shape[1], height=rgb.shape[0])
634:             where = f"+{int(self.pos[0])}+{int(self.pos[1])}" if self.pos else ""
635:             self.root.geometry(f"{rgb.shape[1]}x{rgb.shape[0]}{where}")
636:         else:
637:             self.canvas.itemconfig(self.item, image=photo)
638:         self.canvas.image = photo
639:         self.root.update()
640:         k, self.key = self.key, None
641:         return k
642: 
643:     def close(self) -> None:
644:         if self.ok and not self.closed:
645:             self.closed = True
646:             try:
647:                 self.root.destroy()
648:             except Exception:                                     # noqa: BLE001
649:                 pass
650: 
651: 
652: def roi_for(cx: float, cy: float, r: float, sw: int, sh: int,
653:             pad_x: float = 1.60, pad_up: float = 1.60,
654:             pad_down: float = 3.05) -> dict:
655:     """The capture box, in ABSOLUTE screen coordinates.
656: 
657:     Shape is deliberately narrow and tall:
658: 
659:         horizontal  +-1.60 R   nothing exists past 1.42 R (protrusion ring)
660:         above       + 1.60 R   nothing above the target either
661:         below       + 3.05 R   the waiting knife spans 2.24 R .. 2.86 R
662: 
663:     The old value of 2.35 R below the centre chopped the waiting knife in half,
664:     which would have silently broken any launch/flight measurement.
665:     """
666:     x0 = int(max(0, cx - pad_x * r))
667:     x1 = int(min(sw, cx + pad_x * r))
668:     y0 = int(max(0, cy - pad_up * r))
669:     y1 = int(min(sh, cy + pad_down * r))
670:     return {"left": x0, "top": y0, "width": x1 - x0, "height": y1 - y0}
671: 
672: 
673: def place_preview(bbox: dict, sw: int, sh: int, scale: float):
674:     """Put the preview window somewhere that does NOT overlap the capture box.
675: 
676:     If it overlaps, MSS screenshots the preview of the game instead of the game.
677:     That is a feedback loop, and it is the kind of bug that looks like 'the
678:     tracker is drunk' rather than 'the window is in the way'.
679:     """
680:     pw = int(bbox["width"] * scale)
681:     ph = int(bbox["height"] * scale)
682:     m = 10
683:     x0, y0 = bbox["left"], bbox["top"]
684:     x1, y1 = x0 + bbox["width"], y0 + bbox["height"]
685: 
686:     def free(x: int, y: int) -> bool:
687:         if x < 0 or y < 0 or x + pw > sw or y + ph > sh:
688:             return False
689:         return (x + pw <= x0) or (x >= x1) or (y + ph <= y0) or (y >= y1)
690: 
691:     for cand in ((x1 + m, y0), (x0 - pw - m, y0),
692:                  (x0, y1 + m), (x0, y0 - ph - m),
693:                  (sw - pw - m, sh - ph - m)):
694:         if free(*cand):
695:             return cand
696:     return max(0, sw - pw - m), max(0, sh - ph - m)
697: 
698: 
699: def main() -> int:
700:     ap = argparse.ArgumentParser()
701:     ap.add_argument("--cx", type=float, default=None)
702:     ap.add_argument("--cy", type=float, default=None)
703:     ap.add_argument("--r", type=float, default=None)
704:     ap.add_argument("--preview", action="store_true",
705:                     help="also open the captured-image preview window "
706:                          "(off by default: the HUD draws on the game instead)")
707:     ap.add_argument("--no-hud", action="store_true",
708:                     help="do not draw the overlay on the game")
709:     ap.add_argument("--no-wda", action="store_true",
710:                     help="do not hide the overlay from screen capture "
711:                          "(needed to screenshot-check the overlay geometry)")
712:     ap.add_argument("--hud-fps", type=float, default=30.0,
713:                     help="overlay redraw rate (default 30)")
714:     ap.add_argument("--bench", type=float, default=None,
715:                     help="run N seconds with no preview and report timings")
716:     ap.add_argument("--duration", type=float, default=0.0,
717:                     help="stop after N seconds (0 = run until quit)")
718:     ap.add_argument("--flight-t", type=float, default=DEFAULT_FLIGHT_T)
719:     ap.add_argument("--outdir", default="recordings")
720:     ap.add_argument("--quiet", action="store_true")
721:     ap.add_argument("--wait", type=float, default=90.0,
722:                     help="seconds to wait for the target to appear (0 = give up at once)")
723:     ap.add_argument("--preview-scale", type=float, default=0.6)
724:     ap.add_argument("--ring", type=int, default=20,
725:                     help="frames kept in the dump ring buffer (RAM scales with r^2)")
726:     ap.add_argument("--pad-x", type=float, default=1.60,
727:                     help="ROI half-width, in units of R")
728:     ap.add_argument("--pad-up", type=float, default=1.60,
729:                     help="ROI above centre, in units of R")
730:     ap.add_argument("--pad-down", type=float, default=3.05,
731:                     help="ROI below centre, in units of R (waiting knife needs 2.86)")
732:     ap.add_argument("--max-fps", type=float, default=60.0,
733:                     help="cap the loop rate; 0 = uncapped (will peg a core)")
734:     args = ap.parse_args()
735:     args.no_preview = not args.preview
736: 
737:     os.makedirs(args.outdir, exist_ok=True)
738:     stamp = time.strftime("%Y%m%d_%H%M%S")
739: 
740:     if args.bench:
741:         args.no_preview = True
742:         args.no_hud = True
743:         args.duration = args.bench
744: 
745:     sct = mss.MSS() if hasattr(mss, "MSS") else mss.mss()
746:     mon = sct.monitors[1]
747:     sw, sh = mon["width"], mon["height"]
748:     print(f"[screen] {sw} x {sh}")
749: 
750:     # ---- calibration ----------------------------------------------------- #
751:     if args.cx is not None and args.cy is not None and args.r is not None:
752:         cx, cy, r = args.cx, args.cy, args.r
753:         print(f"[locate] manual centre ({cx:.1f}, {cy:.1f}) radius {r:.1f}")
754:     else:
755:         deadline = time.time() + args.wait
756:         last_note = 0.0
757:         cx = cy = r = None
758:         while True:
759:             full = np.array(sct.grab(mon))[:, :, :3].copy()
760:             got = find_target(full, verbose=False)
761:             if got is not None:
762:                 cx, cy, r = got
763:                 print(f"[locate] centre ({cx:.1f}, {cy:.1f})  radius {r:.1f}")
764:                 b_ = full[:, :, 0].astype(np.int16)
765:                 r_ = full[:, :, 2].astype(np.int16)
766:                 sky_pct = 100.0 * float(((b_ > r_ + 25) & (b_ > 90)).mean())
767:                 print(f"[locate] screen is {sky_pct:.1f}% sky "
768:                       f"(game frames run 40-60%)")
769:                 break
770:             now = time.time()
771:             if args.wait <= 0 or now > deadline:
772:                 b_ = full[:, :, 0].astype(np.int16)
773:                 r_ = full[:, :, 2].astype(np.int16)
774:                 sky_pct = 100.0 * float(((b_ > r_ + 25) & (b_ > 90)).mean())
775:                 print("ERROR: could not locate the target automatically.")
776:                 find_target(full, verbose=True)
777:                 print(f"       screen is only {sky_pct:.1f}% sky -- the game target")
778:                 print("       does not appear to be visible.")
779:                 print("       Alternatively pass --cx --cy --r from a screenshot.")
780:                 return 2
781:             if now - last_note > 4.0:
782:                 last_note = now
783:                 print(f"[wait] looking for the target... "
784:                       f"{int(deadline - now)}s left")
785:             time.sleep(0.6)
786: 
787:     with open(os.path.join(_PROJECT_ROOT, "measurements", "calibration.json"),
788:               "w", encoding="utf-8") as fh:
789:         json.dump({"cx": cx, "cy": cy, "r": r,
790:                    "screen": [sw, sh], "taken": stamp}, fh, indent=2)
791: 
792:     # ---- ROI ------------------------------------------------------------- #
793:     bbox = roi_for(cx, cy, r, sw, sh, args.pad_x, args.pad_up, args.pad_down)
794:     x0, y0 = bbox["left"], bbox["top"]
795:     print(f"[roi] {bbox['width']} x {bbox['height']} at ({x0}, {y0})  "
796:           f"= {100.0 * bbox['width'] * bbox['height'] / (sw * sh):.1f}% of screen")
797: 
798:     # A still picture of exactly what will be captured, drawn on the full screen.
799:     # Written BEFORE the preview window exists, so it cannot photograph itself.
800:     try:
801:         snap = np.array(sct.grab(mon))[:, :, :3].copy()
802:         cv2.rectangle(snap, (bbox["left"], bbox["top"]),
803:                       (bbox["left"] + bbox["width"], bbox["top"] + bbox["height"]),
804:                       (0, 255, 0), 2)
805:         for label, org in (("CAPTURE ROI", (bbox["left"] + 8, bbox["top"] + 22)),):
806:             cv2.putText(snap, label, org, cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.7, (0, 0, 0), 4)
807:             cv2.putText(snap, label, org, cv2.FONT_HERSHEY_SIMPLEX, 0.7, (0, 255, 0), 2)
808:         cv2.imwrite(os.path.join(_PROJECT_ROOT, "measurements", "tracking_area.png"),
809:                     snap)
810:         print("[roi] wrote measurements/tracking_area.png")
811:     except Exception as exc:                                      # noqa: BLE001
812:         print(f"[roi] snapshot skipped ({exc})")
813: 
814:     preview = Preview(args.preview_scale,
815:                       place_preview(bbox, sw, sh, args.preview_scale),
816:                       enabled=not args.no_preview)
817:     hud = Hud(sw, sh, enabled=not args.no_hud, use_wda=not args.no_wda)
818:     hud.verify(sct, mon)
819: 
820:     cxl, cyl = cx - x0, cy - y0
821:     geo = build_geometry(cxl, cyl, r)
822:     mx_tex, my_tex = geo["tex"]
823:     mx_pro, my_pro = geo["pro"]
824: 
825:     # corridor between the target and the waiting knife
826:     cor_y0 = int(cyl + r * 1.02)
827:     cor_y1 = int(min(bbox["height"], cyl + r * 1.95))
828:     cor_x0 = int(max(0, cxl - 0.22 * r))
829:     cor_x1 = int(min(bbox["width"], cxl + 0.22 * r))
830: 
831:     # ---- state ----------------------------------------------------------- #
832:     prev_tex = prev_pro = None
833:     angle = 0.0
834:     angle_hist = collections.deque(maxlen=120)     # (t, angle)
835:     last_t = None
836:     flight_t = args.flight_t
837:     ring = collections.deque(maxlen=max(1, args.ring))
838:     rows = []
839:     fps_t0 = time.perf_counter()
840:     fps_n = 0
841:     fps_shown = 0.0
842:     last_show = 0.0
843:     show_spokes = False
844:     last_hud = 0.0
845:     hk = {}
846:     hud_period = 1.0 / max(1.0, args.hud_fps)
847:     omega_fit = 0.0
848:     t_start = time.perf_counter()
849: 
850:     # --- FIX 1: sign normalisation ---
851:     sign_decided = False
852:     sign = 1.0
853:     sign_buffer = []
854: 
855:     # --- FIX 2: target-lost detection ---
856:     target_lost = False
857:     target_lost_since = 0.0
858:     TARGET_LOST_THRESHOLD = 0.30
859: 
860:     # --- FIX 3: periodic re-locate ---
861:     last_relocate = t_start
862:     RELOCATE_PERIOD = 0.50
863: 
864:     csv_path = os.path.join(args.outdir, f"live_{stamp}.csv")
865:     csv_fh = open(csv_path, "w", newline="", encoding="utf-8")
866:     writer = csv.writer(csv_fh)
867:     writer.writerow(["t", "dt_ms", "fps", "angle_polar_deg", "dtheta_deg",
868:                      "omega_inst_dps", "omega_fit_dps", "conf_tex", "sharp_tex",
869:                      "conf_pro", "n_obstacles", "widest_gap_deg",
870:                      "widest_gap_game_deg", "corridor_motion"])
871: 
872:     timings = collections.defaultdict(list)
873:     _where = ("overlay on the game" if hud.ok else "headless")
874:     if preview.ok and not args.no_preview:
875:         _where += " + preview window"
876:     print(f"[run] {_where}.  F10 stop | F9 dump | F8 spokes")
877: 
878:     try:
879:         while True:
880:             t_now = time.perf_counter()
881:             if args.duration and t_now - t_start > args.duration:
882:                 break
883: 
884:             t_a = time.perf_counter()
885:             raw = sct.grab(bbox)
886:             frame = np.frombuffer(raw.bgra, dtype=np.uint8).reshape(
887:                 raw.height, raw.width, 4)[:, :, :3].copy()
888:             t_b = time.perf_counter()
889: 
890:             gray = cv2.cvtColor(frame, cv2.COLOR_BGR2GRAY)
891:             t_c = time.perf_counter()
892: 
893:             p_tex = polar(gray, mx_tex, my_tex)
894:             p_pro = polar(gray, mx_pro, my_pro)
895:             t_d = time.perf_counter()
896: 
897:             sig_tex = signature_from_polar(p_tex)
898:             sig_pro = signature_from_polar(p_pro)
899: 
900:             dtheta = 0.0
901:             conf_tex = sharp_tex = 0.0
902:             conf_pro = 0.0
903:             if prev_tex is not None and sig_tex is not None and prev_tex is not None:
904:                 lag, conf_tex, sharp_tex = circular_lag(prev_tex, sig_tex)
905:                 dtheta = lag * (360.0 / N_THETA)
906: 
907:             if prev_pro is not None and sig_pro is not None:
908:                 lag2, conf_pro, _ = circular_lag(prev_pro, sig_pro)
909:                 # protrusion ring is the fallback when the texture is flat
910:                 # (bullseye skin has no angular texture at all)
911:                 if conf_tex < MIN_CONF and conf_pro > conf_tex:
912:                     dtheta = lag2 * (360.0 / N_THETA)
913:                     conf_tex = conf_pro

1: # Knife timing & impact geometry — measured
2: 
3: Date: 2026-11-16
4: Source: `gameplay1.mp4` — 1916×868, 30.000 fps, 1409 frames, 46.97 s
5: Target centre (962.78, 246.65), radius **121.76 px** (auto-detected, 25-frame sample)
6: 
7: ---
8: 
9: ## 1. The knife flight time — measured: **NO. Cannot be done from this clip.**
10: 
11: This was attempted three different ways. All three failed, and the reasons are structural,
12: not a matter of trying harder.
13: 
14: ### Attempt A — "the waiting knife disappears when you throw"
15: **Result: impossible by design.** A knife is *always* in the waiting slot. The game
16: reloads it instantly, so there is no frame where the slot is empty. Measured waiting-slot
17: occupancy was flat at **0.07 ± 0.01** for all 1409 frames — no drop, ever.
18: 
19: ### Attempt B — count obstacles in a ring outside the target, detect the +1 step
20: **Result: unusable.** Ring occupancy oscillates smoothly between 2.4 and 9.4 (**no step
21: structure at all**) because the handles sweep through the ring as the target rotates.
22: A landing is a +1 that is smaller than the rotation-induced swing.
23: 
24: ### Attempt C — background-model the sky corridor between target and waiting knife,
25: then track the flying blade
26: **Result: swamped.** 886 of 1409 frames registered as "something moving" (105 separate
27: runs). The corridor is *not* empty sky: as the target rotates, every stuck knife that
28: points downward sweeps through it once per revolution. Per-frame motion counts were
29: p50 = 586, p99 = 1887 out of 3531 corridor pixels — the flying knife is a 3–4 frame
30: transient inside a continuous 5–11 px/frame sweep. Not separable.
31: 
32: ### The arithmetic that kills it regardless
33: 
34: | Quantity | Value |
35: |---|---|
36: | Video frame interval | **33.3 ms** |
37: | Plausible knife flight time | 100–200 ms |
38: | Frames available during flight | **3–6** |
39: | Error from frame quantisation alone | **±33 ms** |
40: | ⇒ relative error on T | **±17 % to ±33 %** |
41: 
42: At 321 °/s, a 17 % error on a 130 ms flight is **≈7° of angular error**. The entire
43: usable window on a tight gap is 25 ms. The measurement is the same size as the thing
44: being measured.
45: 
46: **Conclusion: T cannot be derived from a 30 fps recording. Anyone who claims otherwise
47: is lying or measuring something else.**
48: 
49: ### What replaces it — the closed loop
50: 
51: T is not needed in advance. It is *learned live, in 2 throws*, from our own click
52: timestamps — which a recording does not have:
53: 
54: ```
55: click (t_c, known to us)  ->  launch delay  ->  flight  ->  stick (t_s, observed)
56: 
57: T_total = t_s - t_c
58: ```
59: 
60: After each throw, compare the *predicted* landing angle with the *observed* one:
61: 
62: ```
63: error_deg = observed_landing_angle - 180°
64: ΔT        = error_deg / ω
65: T_total  -= ΔT
66: ```
67: 
68: This single scalar absorbs **input latency + browser event delay + launch animation +
69: flight time + render latency** — everything we cannot model and do not need to.
70: It is strictly better than measuring the flight alone, because the launch delay
71: (the part the user suspects is deliberate) is included automatically.
72: 
73: ---
74: 
75: ## 2. Knife angular width — measured: **8.03°**
76: 
77: Measured on **1983 object samples across 235 frames**, at impact radius r = R.
78: 
79: Method: annulus r ∈ [1.12R, 1.45R]; background test `B > R+25 and B > 90` (blue sky);
80: everything else is an object. Angular widths scaled from the ring's mean radius back to R.
81: 
82: | Statistic | Value |
83: |---|---|
84: | **median** | **8.03°** |
85: | p10 / p90 | 5.14° / 8.35° |
86: | min / max (valid frames) | 1.93° / 25.06° |
87: 
88: Values near 8° are lone knives; the 20–25° outliers are apples.
89: 
90: > **This corrects an earlier working assumption of 16°.** The knife is *half* as wide
91: > as previously budgeted — which doubles every safety margin in the project.
92: 
93: Scaling check: 6.2° measured at mean ring radius 1.285R = 156 px → 16.9 px of physical
94: width → **7.9° at r = R = 122 px**. Consistent.
95:

98: ## 3. Free gaps — measured distribution
99: 
100: | Percentile | Gap width |
101: |---|---|
102: | p10 | 5.0° |
103: | p25 | 5.3° |
104: | p50 | **16.75°** |
105: | p75 | **40.25°** |
106: | p90 | **71.25°** |
107: 
108: The p10/p25 values of ~5° are bark ridges between knife positions, not usable gaps.
109: The practical picture: **the median free gap is ~17°, and the best gap on a busy
110: 10-knife level is typically 38–72°.**
111:

114: ## 4. Safe timing window — the number that decides feasibility
115: 
116: `window = (gap − 8.03°) / ω`
117: 
118: ### ω = 194.5 °/s (slow tier, 0.540 rev/s)
119: 
120: | Gap | Window | @60 Hz |
121: |---|---|---|
122: | 16° | 41.0 ms | 2.5 frames |
123: | 20° | 61.5 ms | 3.7 frames |
124: | 30° | 112.9 ms | 6.8 frames |
125: | 38° | 154.1 ms | 9.2 frames |
126: | 50° | 215.8 ms | 12.9 frames |
127: | 72° | 328.9 ms | 19.7 frames |
128: 
129: ### ω = 321.2 °/s (fast tier, 0.892 rev/s)
130: 
131: | Gap | Window | @60 Hz |
132: |---|---|---|
133: | 16° | 24.8 ms | 1.5 frames |
134: | 20° | 37.3 ms | 2.2 frames |
135: | 30° | 68.4 ms | 4.1 frames |
136: | 38° | 93.3 ms | 5.6 frames |
137: | 50° | 130.7 ms | 7.8 frames |
138: | 72° | 199.2 ms | 11.9 frames |
139: 
140: **Verdict: the game is comfortable.** Even in the worst realistic case — fast tier,
141: the thinnest usable gap — there is 25 ms. With sub-frame prediction the achievable
142: firing accuracy is ~1–2 ms. That is a 12× margin at the worst point, and 40× on a
143: typical gap.
144: 
145: Earlier feasibility planning was pessimistic because it used a 16° knife. It is 8°.

151: ### 5.1 The target changes appearance between levels

153: Any detector that keys on "wood colour" breaks on the next level.
154: The blue-background obstacle test (used above) is appearance-independent and works on
155: both — that is why it was chosen.
156: 
157: ### 5.2 There is a UI flow the bot must drive, not just a throw button
158: The overlay frame shows: `1/3` level counter, a row of ~12 knife icons (stack), a **green
159: GO button**, a **SHOP**, a **CASHOUT** button, a **DIFFICULTY EASY** selector, a
160: **BET** stepper, and a reload/refresh icon.
161: 
162: So a complete run is: press GO → throw 10 → handle level complete → next level →
163: repeat to 16–17 knives. The throw is the easy part; the state machine is the part that
164: breaks silently.

## 2. What `live_track.py` actually does — in plain terms

It is **an observer. Nothing else.** 1277 lines, zero clicks, zero keypresses into the game.

**Pipeline, per frame:**
1. MSS grabs the cropped ROI (`1.60R` left/right, `1.60R` up, `3.05R` down) — about 11.5% of the screen
2. Two polar unwraps at 1440 bins (0.25°): texture ring `0.55–0.92R`, protrusion ring `0.95–1.42R`
3. `circular_lag()` between consecutive signatures → `dtheta`
4. Unwrapped angle → least-squares slope over the last 0.35 s → `omega_fit` (deg/s)
5. Sky mask remapped onto the protrusion ring → occupancy → `runs_of()` finds knives, `gaps_of()` finds free arcs
6. Widest gap + `omega × flight_t` → "ghost gap" (where a gap will be in 150 ms)
7. HUD overlay: click-through Tk window, `WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE`, box + circle + tick marks + gap labels + LIVE text
8. CSV row per frame; ring buffer dump on hotkey; F8/F9/F10 global hotkeys

**What is genuinely proven working** (from `LIVE_HARNESS_REPORT.md`, not my opinion):
- omega live **194.2 °/s** vs offline **194.5 °/s** — 0.15% agreement
- two-tier speed ramp reproduced (78/22 split)
- overlay aligned to **1 px** at 125% DPI
- overlay invisible to MSS (WDA verified pixel-level)
- fps 34–56, dt 17–28 ms

That part is real. The measurement core is good.

## 3. What is actually broken — brutal list

### Blockers

**3.1 `measure_latency.py` cannot start at all.**
It imports seven names that do not exist in `live_track.py`:

| Imported | Reality |
|---|---|
| `make_polar_maps` | real name is `build_geometry` |
| `detect_rotation_and_obstacles` | does not exist |
| `periodic_relocate_check` | does not exist |
| `draw_status` | does not exist |
| `draw_click_through_overlay` | does not exist |
| `get_window_handle_excluding_capture` | does not exist |
| `DEFAULT_RADIUS` | does not exist |

Plus `roi_for(cx, cy, r)` — real signature is `roi_for(cx, cy, r, sw, sh, ...)` → TypeError.

Result: `ImportError` → `sys.exit(1)`. **Phase 1.1 as written is dead on arrival.** I wrote it against an imagined API instead of the real one. That's my error, and it's the kind you told me not to make.

**3.2 My key handling would spam F11/F12 into your browser.**
I wrote `while not pydirectinput.keyDown('f2')`. `pydirectinput.keyDown()` **sends** a keystroke — it does not **read** state. So that line fires F2 thousands of times a second into whatever window has focus, and `check_quit_keys` does the same with **F11 — the browser fullscreen toggle**. Your browser would flicker in and out of fullscreen continuously.

`live_track.py` already does this correctly in `_vk_pressed()` using `GetAsyncKeyState`. I ignored the pattern that was sitting 400 lines up in the file I was reading.

### In `live_track.py` itself

**3.3 Angle is double-counted after sign lock.**
Line 924 advances `angle += dtheta`. Line 958 advances it **again** with the signed `dtheta`.
- If `sign = +1` → logged angle advances **2× too fast**
- If `sign = -1` → advances by **zero**, angle freezes

`omega_fit` survives because it's fitted from `angle_hist` samples taken *before* the second add (line 930). But **`angle_polar_deg` in every CSV is garbage after ~0.5 s.** Anyone doing angle analysis off those logs is reading noise.

**3.4 `omega_fit *= sign` compounds.**
When the lstsq branch is skipped (fewer than 6 points in window), `omega_fit` keeps its previous *already-flipped* value and gets multiplied by `sign` again that frame. On a CCW run (`sign = -1`) it alternates ± every frame → HUD ω and ghost lead flip-flop.

**3.5 The sign lock is the wrong tool.**
`circular_lag` sign is deterministic — it's the direction of motion, not random. The report says the earlier run "landed on a different peak" — that's a symptom of a bad start, not a reason to multiply by ±1 forever afterwards. Locking a sign once and then multiplying in place is exactly what created 3.3 and 3.4.

**3.6 The HUD circle sits inside the measured band.**
The class docstring says *"NEVER draw between 0.92R and 1.42R"* — then the code draws a circle at exactly `1.0R` and knife ticks at `1.44–1.50R`. It only doesn't matter because `WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE` hides it from MSS.

**That makes WDA load-bearing for correctness, not decoration.** If a Windows update or GPU driver change makes `SetWindowDisplayAffinity` fail, the tracker starts measuring its own cyan circle as a knife ring. `verify()` only checks a 16×16 corner *outside* the ROI — it would never catch ink contamination *inside* it.

**3.7 `target_lost` does not gate the angle integrator.**
`dtheta` keeps integrating into `angle` during blindness. The CSV is marked `-1` so it doesn't poison analysis, but the internal angle drifts while blind. Contradicts the "never log blindness as data" principle the file claims to follow.

**3.8 `corridor_motion` never sees the waiting knife.**
`cor_y0 = cyl + 1.02r`, `cor_y1 = cyl + 1.95r`. The waiting knife lives at **2.24R–2.86R** (that's why `pad_down = 3.05`). So the corridor measures "something crossed the space between target and knife", not "the knife left the slot". Usable as a *launch* detector — but it also cannot tell the flying blade from a stuck knife sweeping through during rotation, which is precisely attempt C that already failed in `KNIFE_TIMING_AND_GEOMETRY.md`.

## 4. Where I think the plan is ordered wrong

The PRD runs Phase 1 = latency, Phase 2 = actuator. **That order is impossible.** You cannot measure click→land latency without something that clicks. `measure_latency.py` *is* an actuator with a stopwatch. So 1 and 2 are the same phase, and the file has to be written against the real `live_track.py` API, not a fantasy one.

Also: FR-ACT-02 demands "fire within ±1 ms, verified via audio sync". You don't have a high-speed camera or an audio rig. That number cannot be verified on this hardware, and it doesn't need to be — at 321 °/s, 5 ms of jitter is 1.6°, which is fine. Keep the target honest: **±5 ms measured, not ±1 ms imagined.**

And the real priority is not the actuator. It's this line from your own report:

> **frames with ≥ 8 knives visible:** 0.0% / 0.0% / 56.2% / 62.2% / 19.5%

Best case, the observer saw the target with all knives **62% of the time**. The three fixes are written but **have never once run live**. Putting a perfectly timed clicker on an observer that's blind half the time throws knives into walls at 4 ms precision.

**Order should be:**
1. Prove the observer sees the target ≥95% of frames across a level transition — with the fixes active, with real CSVs

Now, KEY REALIZATION about the L1-L60 grid: The user's mental model was to describe positions as L1-L60. But the log ROTATES. So a fixed L-grid on the screen is useless as a target reference unless you know the log's current rotation. If L1 is fixed at screen-top, then "the gap is at L20" means a screen-fixed direction, not a log-fixed position. For aiming, what matters is: at the moment of impact, is there free space at screen-bottom (180°)?

That's the crucial insight: **you don't need the log's absolute rotation at all.** You only need to know, right now, whether the arc at screen-bottom (180°) is blocked, and when the next free gap will arrive at 180°. The current live_track predicts "ghost gap = widest gap + ω·T" in polar coordinates — that's for a single chosen gap, not for the fixed impact point.

That's a design error worth flagging: the bot should compute **time until the impact point (180°) becomes free**, i.e. for each gap, the time when that gap's angular interval covers 180°. That's the actual firing condition. Currently it tracks the widest gap and where it'll be — which is a different question and requires inverse kinematics.

Let me formalize:
- Occupancy in polar coords (log-fixed, rotating with log).
- Impact direction in polar coords = 180° - θ_log, where θ_log is log rotation (since polar coords rotate with log).
- Actually if polar signature is log-fixed, then the impact point moves through the polar map at -ω.
- So: gap centre g, width w. The gap covers impact when |wrap(g - (180 - θ))| < w/2... 

Hmm, need care with conventions. In live_track, `polar_to_game(a) = (a + 90) % 360`, so polar 0° = game 270° (left)? Let's see: game convention up=0, clockwise. Polar convention +x=0, clockwise (since y down in images, +y is down, so angle measured from +x toward +y = clockwise). `polar_to_game(a) = a + 90`. So polar a=0 → game 90 = right. Yes: polar 0 = right = game 90. Good.

Impact is at game 180 (bottom) → polar 90.

So the impact point in polar coords is a=90. As the log rotates clockwise (game angle increases), the polar signature... hmm. If the log rotates clockwise on screen, then a feature at polar angle a moves to a+ω·dt in polar coords. So the pattern shifts positive. Then a fixed screen direction (polar 90) corresponds to pattern angle 90 - ω·t.

So to know when a gap at polar position g will be over the impact point: need g ≡ 90 - ω·t → t = (90 - g)/ω.

Currently live_track computes `ghost = widest[0] + widest[1]/2 + omega_fit*flight_t` — that's where the gap centre will BE after flight time, in polar coords. To fire correctly you want the gap centre to be at the impact point at impact time: g + ω·T ≡ 90 → T = (90 - g)/ω... and you fire now if T ≈ T_total. So the condition is `((90 - g_center)/ω mod 360/ω) ≈ T_total`. The code's ghost line is the reverse: it draws where the gap will be, not when it will reach 90. Both are equivalent only if you set ghost == 90. So the display is a "where" indicator, and the user would have to visually judge. For the bot, must be a "time" computation.

11:

14: genuine valley between histogram modes.

32: **Transitions** between the two speeds are smooth ramps of roughly 0.5–1 s, not instant
33: steps. There is a band between ~205 and ~260 °/s where the speed is *unknown* — a bot
34: should not throw blind inside it.

39: 
40: ## 2. How much to trust it
41: 
42: ### Good
43: 
44: - Two independent estimators (radial-signature correlation, and per-ring correlation)
45:   agree to a **median of 0.005°**, 95th percentile 0.020°.
46: - Only **6 frames out of 1370 (0.44%)** disagreed by more than 2°.
47: - Centre refined by maximising correlation rather than by shape: mean confidence
48:   **0.78 → 0.90**. The centre crosshair is visibly dead-centre on the log.
49: - 97.3% of frames passed the confidence gate.
50: - `find_speed.py` runs a self-test at startup that *proves* the sign convention and
51:   sub-pixel accuracy. There is no sign bug in the output.
52: 
53: ### Not good — be aware
54: 
55: - **226 of 1408 frames (16%) needed repair.** The recording has heavy capture jitter: the
56:   encoder duplicates frames, then catches up with a double step. Fixed by integrating angle
57:   first and differentiating over a 0.5 s window (correct treatment for a noisy incremental
58:   signal), but it proves the 30 fps file is a poor sample.
59:   **Re-record at 60 fps constant frame rate (OBS, CFR) for tighter numbers.**
60: - **The two "reversals" at t = 39.17 s and 39.37 s are probably not reversals.** The log
61:   dips to zero, goes negative for ~1 s, then recovers — the shape of a **round restart**,
62:   not a direction change. Flagged as uncertain, not claimed.
63: - **9.6 ms/frame offline.** This includes the cross-check estimator; it is not the
64:   real-time path. The lean path has not been timed yet and no number should be quoted for
65:   it until it is.
66: - 30 fps recording of a 60 fps game. The speed values transfer (angles are scale-invariant)
67:   but the *timing resolution* does not.
68: 
69: ### The genuinely good news
70: 
71: At 321 °/s and 60 Hz, a 30° gap gives a **~44 ms window — about 2.6 frames**. The game is
72: much slower than the worst case assumed in early planning. The timing problem is
73: comfortably solvable.
74: 
75: ---
76: 
77: ## 3. Method — why classical CV and not an AI model
78: 
79: The task is not "recognise the log". It is *"how many degrees did the log rotate between
80: frame t and frame t+1, to within ±0.3°"*. That is metrology, not perception.
81: 
82: The wood grain, bark cracks and rim shading form a natural **optical encoder**. Pipeline:
83: 
84: 1. **Locate the log** — colour mask → dominant warm blob → vectorised radial scan → robust
85:    median radius (rejects protruding knives) → algebraic least-squares circle fit, iterated.
86: 2. **Refine the centre** — grid search for the centre that maximises inter-frame correlation
87:    (coarse 2 px, fine 0.5 px). A centre error `e` injects a once-per-revolution wobble of
88:    roughly `e/r` radians; 12 px at r = 122 px was ~5.6° of corruption.
89: 3. **Polar unwrap** an annulus, `r ∈ [0.55 R, 0.92 R]`. The inner cut deliberately excludes
90:    the multiplier text at the log's centre.
91: 4. **Collapse to a 1-D signature** `s(θ)` — per-ring DC removal and equalisation, then mean
92:    across radius.
93: 5. **Circular cross-correlation** between consecutive signatures, FFT-based, with parabolic
94:    sub-bin interpolation.
95: 6. **Cross-check** every frame with a second estimator that correlates each radius ring
96:    separately instead of averaging first.
97: 7. **Integrate → deglitch → differentiate over a window** to defeat capture jitter.
98: 8. **Cluster** the speed histogram into tiers, requiring a real valley between modes.
99: 
100: Why not a neural network:
101: 
102: | | classical correlation | CNN / segmentation |
103: |---|---|---|
104: | accuracy | 0.05–0.3° | ~±1° (mask boundary noise: 1 px = 0.43° at r = 132) |
105: | cost / frame | ~1–2 ms (lean path, estimated) | 5–30 ms |
106: | training data | none needed | none available |
107: | failure mode | explicit confidence score | opaque |
108: | budget @ 60 Hz | 16.7 ms total | inference alone can exceed it |
109: 
110: A neural net is the right tool for a different job: producing a **one-time ground-truth
111: mask** of the log, offline. Not for the control loop.
112: 
113: ---
114:

116: 
117: These were found while building the pipeline and should be fixed before any coordinate is
118: reused.
119: 
120: 1. **Four different image sizes across the source material** — `download.jpg` 1917×1077,

127: 
128: 3. **Knife tip recorded as both (954, 666) and (959, 657)** — 9 px apart.
129: 
130: 4. **The sixteen "centre to corner" values are mislabelled.** Each is the distance from a
131:    *screen corner* to the object's centre — pure Pythagoras, zero new information.
132:    Verified 4/4 exactly for the log: √(949² + 390²) = 1026.0, etc. Labels read as
133:    object-corner distances and will mislead anyone reusing them. Drop them from the spec.

137:    left → ≈ **181.3°**. A **13 px / 5.6° contradiction** between the table and the drawing.

# C. The finding that matters most: the three fixes broke the core measurement

I counted sign behaviour and speed distribution per run. This is not opinion:

| run | samples | % positive | sign flips | in slow tier (150–240) | in fast tier (280–360) | **>400 °/s (impossible)** |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 11:09:20 | 1433 | 78.0 | 3 | **809** | **239** | **0** |
| 11:10:12 | 1730 | 12.5 | 5 | **1213** | **251** | **0** |
| 11:12:58 | 532 | 22.0 | 14 | 365 | 0 | 0 |
| **11:27:11 (fixes active)** | 1589 | 46.6 | 11 | **19** | 80 | **613** |

And the percentiles on the fixed run: **p25 = −392.6, p75 = +395.6, p95 = +661.1**.

194.5 × 2 = 389. 321.2 × 2 = 642. **The fixed run is reading exactly double the true speed.**

**Why — traced in the code:**

```
line 924:  angle = (angle + dtheta) % 360      # add #1
line 930:  angle_hist.append((t_now, angle))   # history sampled here
line 958:  angle = (angle + dtheta_signed)     # add #2, same frame
```

So the history sequence becomes `d₁, 2d₁+d₂, 2d₁+2d₂+d₃ …`. Consecutive differences ≈ **2 × dθ**. The least-squares slope therefore returns **2 ω**. The `omega_fit` you see in the HUD and the CSV is double the truth from the moment the sign locks (~0.5 s in).

The "sign normalisation fix" did not fix the sign. It **doubled the speed** and left the sign still flipping. Before the fix, omega was correct and only inverted. After the fix, omega is 2× and unstable. **That is a regression, and I wrote it.**

**Also confirmed:** `angle_polar_deg` goes 141.29 → 141.29 → 185.85 → … and at the end 103.66 → 90.63 → 77.60 (running *backwards*). The angle column is garbage in that run. Nobody should ever analyse it.

---

# D. Second finding: the "target lost" detector fires while the target is plainly visible

Same run: **65.6 % of frames marked lost** — yet in the frames it *did* accept, obstacles read 8–17:

| n_obstacles | 8 | 9 | 10 | 11 | 12 | 13 | 14 | 15 | 16 |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| frames | 177 | 200 | 188 | 345 | 198 | 149 | 221 | 54 | 56 |

You cannot have 11 knives on a log you claim to be blind to. The `sky_annulus_frac(...) < 0.35` test is the culprit, and it is structurally wrong for this job:

- It samples rings at **1.08 / 1.18 / 1.28 / 1.38 R**. That's exactly where the knives and their handles live — 8 to 14 of them, each ~8° wide plus a handle.
- Behind the log there is **not** sky. Look at either image: the lower half of the annulus lands on **pine trees and mountains**. The top half is sky. So even a perfect lock reads maybe 50–60 %, and a crowded log pushes it lower.
- It was written as a **startup guard** ("is this blob floating in sky, or is it the editor window?"). It is now being reused as a **continuous health check**. Different question, wrong instrument.

That is why the only fixed run is the worst run.

---

# E. What the game actually is — corrected model

Before this read, the mental model was "find the widest gap, track where it goes". That is a human aid, not a firing condition.

A throw is: blade flies **straight up** the vertical line and sticks at the **bottom of the log, 180°**. Therefore:

> The only thing that matters is: **is the arc at 180° free at the instant the blade arrives?**

Not "where is the widest gap". Not "where will the widest gap be in 150 ms".

`live_track.py` draws `ghost = gap_centre + ω·T` — that's *where a gap will be*. The firing condition is the inverse:

```
T_arrive = wrap(impact_polar − gap_centre) / ω     # seconds until this gap reaches 180°
FIRE when T_arrive ≈ T_total  (± margin)
```

Those two are only equivalent if you read the ghost display with your eyes. For a bot they are different arithmetic, and **the current code does not compute the one you need.** That's a design gap, not a bug, but it has to be fixed before any clicker is written.

---

# F. The unknown that decides the whole project: how many knives to 2.00x

Two ladders exist in your own artefacts and **they do not match**:

| Source | Sequence | Step pattern |
|---|---|---|
| `image.png` / overlay screenshot | 1.00, 1.01, 1.03, 1.06, 1.10 | +.01, +.02, +.03, +.04 — **very regular** |
| `gameplay1.mp4` ladder read | 1.01, 1.03, 1.10, 1.19, 1.24, 1.30, 1.35, 1.42, 1.48, 1.56 | irregular |

They agree on the first three values and diverge at the fourth. Two possible readings:

- **If the regular series is the real one:** 1.00, 1.01, 1.03, 1.06, 1.10, 1.15, 1.21, 1.28, 1.36, 1.45, **1.55**, 1.66, 1.78, 1.91, **2.05** → knife 10 = 1.55 (**matches the video's 1.56 almost exactly**), and **2.00x arrives at knife ~14**, not 16–17.
- **If the video ladder is real:** 2.00x is somewhere past 1.85, i.e. **~21–23 knives**.

That's a 14 vs 23 spread, and it changes the number of level transitions from 1 to 2. It changes p^14 vs p^23 and it changes how much state-machine work exists.

**This is answerable in 30 seconds, no code:** open the game, click the `>` arrow on the ladder, screenshot every page. That gives the exact sequence and the exact count. Do that before anything else — it's the cheapest experiment available and it currently blocks every estimate in the PRD.

| Claim | Evidence |
|---|---|

That's real work and it holds. **No need to touch it.**

## But: it is currently lying to you

Look at what `hud.draw()` prints:

```
f"LIVE {fps}fps  w {omega}d/s  conf {conf}  gap {gap}"
```

`omega` there is `omega_fit` — which is **2× wrong right now** (392 instead of 194, 661 instead of 321). So if you watched the HUD and saw roughly double the speeds you expected, that wasn't you misreading it. The overlay was faithfully drawing a wrong number.

**The drawing is correct. The number it's drawing is not.** Two separate things, fixed in two separate places.

---

## The one real defect in the HUD

The class docstring says: *"NEVER draw between 0.92R and 1.42R."* Then it does this:

| Ink | Radius | Verdict |
|---|---|---|
| Capture box | 1.60R h / 1.60R up / 3.05R down | ✅ outside every band |
| **Circle** | **1.00R** | ⚠️ **inside the protrusion estimator annulus (0.95–1.42R)** |
| Obstacle ticks | 1.44–1.50R | ✅ |
| Gap labels | 1.54R | ✅ |
| Spokes / L-labels | 1.44–1.55R / 1.62R | ✅ |
| Status text + dot | outside the ROI entirely | ✅ |

Precise consequence, not hand-waving: the circle is **outside** the occupancy band (1.117–1.42R), so gap detection is safe. It is **inside** the protrusion estimator's annulus, so if WDA ever stops working, a static screen-fixed circle correlates perfectly at zero lag and **pulls the bullseye-skin fallback omega toward zero** — on exactly the levels where that fallback is what's keeping you alive.

And `verify()` cannot catch it: it samples a **16×16 patch at the monitor's top-left corner**, where we never draw anything. A WDA failure is invisible to that test.

**Cheap insurance:** draw the circle at **1.46R** instead of 1.0R. Then every pixel of ink lives at ≥1.44R, and the HUD is provably incapable of contaminating any measurement band — **even if WDA fails entirely.** Correctness stops depending on a Windows API continuing to behave.

---

## What the HUD should show next (and currently doesn't)

Right now it answers *"where is the widest gap, and where will it be in 150 ms?"* That's a question for a human eyeballing it.

The bot needs a different number on screen:

```
TIME TO GAP AT 180°:  0.184 s     ← the only number that decides a throw
T_total:              0.150 s
FIRE IN:              0.034 s     → green when armed
```

Because the blade flies straight up and sticks at the bottom, the firing condition is `wrap(impact − gap_centre) / ω ≈ T_total`. The HUD shows neither of those quantities today. Adding them is a display change only — no new vision work.

---

## So, my verdict

**The cyan geometry HUD: working, verified, keep it.** It's the most finished piece of the project.

1. Circle 1.0R → **1.46R** (makes WDA non-load-bearing)
2. `verify()` → sample a pixel *where we actually draw*, not a corner we never touch
3. Add the **time-to-180°** readout — the display should show the decision, not just the scenery

[3:36] By default, Sleep is actually only accurate to around 15ms intervals, so calling Sleep(1) will way overshoot.
[3:43] We can increase precision using timeBeginPeriod, from mmsystem.h. We now also need to link to winmm.
[3:50] timeBeginPeriod sets the thread timing resolution to a number of milliseconds, so we set it to one since that’s lowest. [...] [3:56] Until Windows 10 version 2004, this set the system-wide timer resolution and therefore increased CPU and power usage even after closing your program, so be sure to call timeEndPeriod with the same value at the end of the program.
[4:09] Since that Windows version this is now handled per-process and is no longer a problem for most users. [...] [4:14] So we calculate the number of milliseconds to sleep by taking the target number of ticks, subtracting the current ticks, then dividing by ticks per millisecond.
[4:22] Then we sleep for that time.
[4:25] Now we can Sleep with millisecond precision, though it’s still inaccurate, often missing by 1 millisecond and occasionally more than that.

## [PowerShell Sleep Duration Accuracy and Windows Timers | xkln.net](https://xkln.net/blog/powershell-sleep-duration-accuracy-and-windows-timers)

Keen readers may have noticed that our minimum valid value for the timer resolution is 0.5ms, but the `timeBeginPeriod` function accepts milliseconds in integers. We have no way of specifying 0.5ms as an integer using milliseconds.

We need to call a different function to get 0.5ms resolution.

### Setting 0.5ms Timer Resolution with PowerShell and NtSetTimerResolution [...] In order to change the timer resolution we need to call two Win32 functions. timeBeginPeriod to set the new resolution, and timeEndPeriod to tell Windows we no longer need our new resolution, which will then set it back to the shortest duration that other programs may have requested, or if there are none, back to the default. [...] By default on Windows systems the timer interrupts fire at intervals of 15.625ms, or 64Hz (64 times a second). The result is that our thread is put to sleep and the CPU interrupt to wake it doesn’t fire until the timer ticks over, which is 15.625ms away. This is how we get an average sleep time of ~15.3ms for a 1 millisecond sleep command.

## [The DRM Flag That Isn't DRM](https://www.ioactive.com/the-drm-flag-that-isnt-drm/)

_SetWindowDisplayAffinity makes a window disappear from screenshots, screen shares, and Recall snapshots._

## **The Pitch, and the Problem with It**
_Unlike a security feature or an implementation of Digital Rights Management (DRM), there is no guarantee that using SetWindowDisplayAffinity … will strictly protect window content._

## **How the Flag Works**
```
BOOL SetWindowDisplayAffinity(
  [in] HWND  hWnd,      // top-level window, must belong to the calling process
  [in] DWORD dwAffinity // the exclusion mode
);
```

Under `WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE`, the window is not in the frame and the desktop behind it shows through, so the capture looks like the application was not running at all.

## **The Actual DRM, for Comparison**
|  |  |  |
|-|-|-|
|  | SetWindowDisplayAffinity | Hardware DRM (protected media path) |
| **Stops a phone camera** | No | No |
| **Who can disable it** | Any code running inside the owning process | No software path; requires defeating the hardware |

## **What Developers Should Do**
On builds older than 19041, **[WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE succeeds and behaves as WDA_MONITOR](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setwindowdisplayaffinity#remarks)** [,](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setwindowdisplayaffinity#remarks) so the window turns black instead of vanishing and the API never mentions the difference.

## [How Windows Screen Capture Exclusion Actually Works](https://www.interviewpilot.in/blog/windows-screen-capture-exclusion-explained/)

## [Why this is possible at all](https://www.interviewpilot.in/blog/windows-screen-capture-exclusion-explained/#why-this-is-possible-at-all)
```
BOOL SetWindowDisplayAffinity(
  HWND   hWnd,
  DWORD  dwAffinity
);
```

## [Where the requirement actually comes from](https://www.interviewpilot.in/blog/windows-screen-capture-exclusion-explained/#where-the-requirement-actually-comes-from)
Before that, Windows only offered `WDA_MONITOR` — a cruder flag that blacked out the window entirely on any secondary output, useful for DRM-protected video playback but useless for something you still want to see and interact with yourself. `WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE` is the newer, more surgical version: exclude from _capture_, not from _display_.

Anything built on this API only works on Windows 10 version 2004 or later, or Windows 11. An application that depends on it either needs to detect the OS version at startup and refuse to run the stealth path, or (more honestly) needs to tell the user up front that this feature is Windows-only.

## [The practical takeaway](https://www.interviewpilot.in/blog/windows-screen-capture-exclusion-explained/#the-practical-takeaway)
If a Windows application claims its window is invisible to screen shares, `SetWindowDisplayAffinity(hwnd, WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE)` is very likely the mechanism, because it's the only supported, non-hacky way to achieve that behavior on modern Windows.

## [Further reading](https://www.interviewpilot.in/blog/windows-screen-capture-exclusion-explained/#further-reading)
Microsoft's own documentation for [`SetWindowDisplayAffinity`](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/windows/win32/api/winuser/nf-winuser-setwindowdisplayaffinity) is short and worth reading directly if you're implementing this yourself — it documents both `WDA_MONITOR` and `WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE`, along with the minimum supported client (Windows 10, version 2004).

# How Invisible Screen Share TechnologyActually Works
## Windows: SetWindowDisplayAffinity
On Windows 10 version 2004 and later, Microsoft provides a function called`SetWindowDisplayAffinity`in the Win32 API.

```
SetWindowDisplayAffinity(hwnd, WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE)
```

When a window has`WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE`set, the DWM excludes it from all capture surfaces.

### What about WDA_MONITOR?
This was the only option before Windows 10 2004.`WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE`is strictly better — it removes the window entirely instead of showing a suspicious black rectangle.

### Requirements and Limitations
**Minimum version:** Windows 10 version 2004 (build 19041) or later. Older versions fall back to WDA_MONITOR.

**Hardware acceleration:** DWM must be enabled (it is by default on all modern Windows). Remote Desktop sessions disable DWM, which breaks the exclusion.

**Virtual machines:** Works in most VM configurations where GPU passthrough or virtual GPU is available. May not work in basic VMs without GPU acceleration.

Research done. Three things changed my assumptions — I'll bake them in:

- **`timeBeginPeriod`** is per-process since Win10 2004, and `Sleep` is still unreliable below a few ms → the correct pattern is **sleep-then-spin**, not sleep.
- **`WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE`** requires **Win10 build 19041+**; on older builds it *succeeds but silently behaves as `WDA_MONITOR`* (black box). Works only with DWM composing — so Remote Desktop silently breaks it.
- **`pydirectinput` exists for DirectX games.** This game is a **browser canvas** — normal Win32 messages. Its whole reason for existing may not apply here. That assumption must be tested, not inherited.

## Three corrections from the web research, baked in

1. **Phase 6.3** — `Sleep` is unreliable below ~2 ms and Windows' default timer is 15.625 ms. The plan specifies **sleep-then-spin** with `perf_counter`, which is the only way to hit sub-millisecond firing without a high-speed camera.
2. **Phase 3.1/§2.6** — `WDA_EXCLUDEFROMCAPTURE` requires Win10 build 19041+; on older builds it **succeeds but silently behaves as `WDA_MONITOR`**. So the overlay's safety can't be assumed — hence moving all ink to ≥1.44R so correctness stops depending on it.
3. **Phase 6.2** — `pydirectinput` exists for **DirectX** games. This is a browser canvas receiving normal Win32 messages, so `SendInput`/`pyautogui` should be tried **first**. The last plan assumed pydirectinput without justification.

---

## What I deliberately did NOT do

- No code edits — `live_track.py` is untouched, still at `c4bf1d6`
- No deletions — junk CSVs are flagged for `recordings/invalid/`, not moved
- No new dependencies — and I flagged that `pydirectinput` already leaked onto C: (§0 rule 6)

---

## The order, in one line

**§Phase 0** (read the ladder — 15 min, manual, kills the biggest unknown) → **§Phase 1** (three deletions, restores correct ω) → **§Phase 2** (instrument, then replace the health test) → then and only then anything else.

Until §Phase 1's acceptance table passes — `p50 |ω| = 194.5 ± 2 %`, **zero** samples above 400 °/s — the observer is not trustworthy and nothing built on top of it can be.

Find window by title containing "Knife Rush" and visible.

Implementation:

```python
import ctypes
from ctypes import wintypes

user32 = ctypes.WinDLL('user32', use_last_error=True)

targets = []
EnumProc = ctypes.WINFUNCTYPE(wintypes.BOOL, wintypes.HWND, wintypes.LPARAM)

def cb(hwnd, lparam):
    if not user32.IsWindowVisible(hwnd):
        return True
    n = user32.GetWindowTextLengthW(hwnd)
    if n == 0:
        return True
    buf = ctypes.create_unicode_buffer(n+1)
    user32.GetWindowTextW(hwnd, buf, n+1)
    title = buf.value
    if 'Knife Rush' in title:
        targets.append((hwnd, title))
    return True

user32.EnumWindows(EnumProc(cb), 0)
print(targets)
```

user32.SetForegroundWindow(hwnd)

time.sleep(0.3)
user32.ShowWindow(hwnd, 3)  # maximize
time.sleep(1.0)
print("foreground now:", user32.GetForegroundWindow())

Design in analyze_run.py:

```python
def local_consistency(deltas, half=15):
    n = len(deltas)
    if n < 3: return float("nan")
    agree = 0; total = 0
    for i, d in enumerate(deltas):
        lo = max(0, i-half); hi = min(n, i+half+1)
        win = deltas[lo:hi]
        med = _pct(win, 50)
        if med == 0: continue
        total += 1
        if d * med > 0: agree += 1
    return 100.0*agree/total if total else float("nan")
```

# PHASE 1 — what we did, and what came out

## The problem we were fixing

The tracker was reporting rotation speed at **exactly 2×** the truth. Evidence from the broken run: `p50 = 394.1 °/s` against a real 194.5, and `613 of 1589` samples above the physical ceiling of 343.5 °/s. Any timing prediction built on that number would fire at half the correct delay — i.e. a guaranteed miss.

## The four code changes

| # | Change | Why |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | **Deleted the duplicate angle advance** (old line 958) | `angle` was advanced in two places. Line 927 added `dtheta`, line 958 added it *again* after the sign multiply. On CW runs that is literally ×2. |
| 2 | **Deleted `omega_fit *= sign` and `omega_inst *= sign`** | These are state variables. Multiplying in place every frame means a `-1` sign flips the value every frame — compounding error, not correcting it. |
| 3 | **Deleted the entire sign-lock mechanism** (`sign_decided`, `sign`, `sign_buffer`, and its resets) | The sign is a *measurement*, not a constant. See the result below — the log reverses. |
| 4 | **Added `omega_stable`** = `warm AND 60 ≤ \|ω\| ≤ 400` | Physically impossible values must never reach the firing logic. |

Plus one thing the plan did **not** predict, which the live data forced:

> **`WARMUP_S = 1.0`** — no measurement is published until 1 full second of unbroken confident frames. The first ~0.85 s after acquisition produced fit values up to **602 °/s** while the least-squares window was still filling. Against a real cap of 343.5, that was pure garbage being logged as data.

## The result — all five acceptance checks

```
C1  p50 |ω| = 195.9  vs  194.5 truth        +0.7 %      PASS
C2  samples above 400 °/s      0 of 714     (was 613/1589) PASS
C3  slow tier (150-240)        78.9 %       > 50 %      PASS
C4  fast tier (280-360)        18.9 %       5-40 %      PASS
C5  local direction consistency 98.7 %      ≥ 95 %      PASS
```

**VERDICT: PASS.** Exit code 0. Source file: `recordings/live_20261117_155446.csv`, 60 s, 1987 rows, 714 tracked.

## Three discoveries that changed the project

1. **The log reverses direction.** 9 clean sign runs in 60 s — 4 CW, 5 CCW, lasting 0.3–9.1 s each. A locked sign would have inverted every prediction after each flip. This is now measured fact, not speculation.
2. **C5 as originally written was an impossible test.** "Monotone over ≥95 % of the run" cannot be satisfied by a game that reverses. I replaced it with *local* direction consistency — compare each frame against its own ±15-frame neighbourhood. That catches real glitches and tolerates real reversals.
3. **The target's big number is the NEXT multiplier, not the current one.** Proof: bet 105 → cashout 108.15 = ×1.03, while the label read 1.06. So cashout = `ladder[n]`, label = `ladder[n+1]`. This is trap T20 now.

I also caught **7 broken command lines in my own plan** (`--no-preview` does not exist — argparse exits 2) and fixed them.

# PHASE 2 — what is in it, and why it's next

## The problem it fixes

**64.1 % of frames were discarded as "lost"** while the log was clearly visible and spinning perfectly. You cannot aim a bot with 36 % of its frames. This is BUG-4.

The cause is one line:

```python
tracking_ok = (len(obs) >= 8 and sky_now >= 0.35)
```

`sky_annulus_frac` samples rings at 1.08–1.38 R — **exactly where knives and their handles live**. And the background is a pine forest, not sky. So the "health check" is measuring the wrong thing in the wrong place, and firing false alarms constantly. Those false alarms then trigger a **full-screen Hough search every 0.5 s**, which is why fps fell from 47 to 35.

## The four steps

| Step | Action |
|---|---|
| **2.1** Instrument | Add CSV columns: `sky_now`, `r`, `cx`, `cy`, `omega_stable`, `lost_reason` (0=none, 1=too few obstacles, 2=sky low, 3=both). Compute every frame, **log only, act on nothing.** |
| **2.2** One diagnostic run | `python live_track.py --duration 120` — you play normally, including one level transition if you can. |
| **2.3** Analyse, then decide | Measure the `sky_now` distribution **during frames we know are good** (≥8 obstacles, stable ω). Pick a threshold with **< 1 % false positives**. Do not guess a threshold before seeing the data. |
| **2.4** Implement + verify | Only then replace the gate. |

Candidate design from the plan — **not to be adopted before the data exists**:

- health = `8 ≤ n_obstacles ≤ 18` **AND** `r` within ±8 % of calibrated `r` **AND** sane `|ω|`
- `sky_annulus_frac` used **only at startup and on explicit re-locate**, never per frame
- **2 consecutive** failing frames before declaring lost (not 1)
- **3 consecutive** failures before a full-screen `find_target`

## Phase 2 acceptance

| Check | Pass |
|---|---|
| `lost_pct` during active play | **< 10 %** (currently **64.1 %**) |
| Frames with ≥8 obstacles marked lost | **0** |
| Full-screen `find_target` calls per 60 s | **< 5** |
| Level transition recovered within | **< 2 s** |

## Why Phase 2 must come before anything else

Every later phase depends on it:

- **Phase 4** (firing maths) needs a continuous angle — gaps destroy the prediction window.
- **Phase 6** (actuator) must not fire on stale data.
- **Phase 8** (miss detection) needs to distinguish "missed" from "lost tracking" — right now it can't.

Cost: one 120-second run from you, plus analysis on my side. Nothing is pushed to git.

**Say go and I'll write the instrumentation.**

# On knife flight speed — what's actually possible

Straight answer, no flattery:

**Flight *time* is measurable. Flight *speed* in real units is not** — the game gives no world scale, so px/s is the only honest unit.

| Quantity | Measurable now? | How |
|---|---|---|
| Flight duration | **Yes**, ±1 frame (~30 ms) | Waiting knife leaves its slot → new obstacle appears on the log |
| Travel speed (px/s) | **Yes** | launcher→rim distance ÷ duration |
| Click→launch latency | **No** | needs the actuator (Phase 6) |
| Real-world m/s | **No** | no world scale exists |

At 26–35 fps and ~150 ms of flight you get only **4–5 samples per throw**, so a single throw can't pin it down. But the flight animation is almost certainly identical every throw, so averaging ~15 throws gives ±30/√15 ≈ **±8 ms**. That's good enough to seed the closed loop.

The measurement is a clean one: the knife slot under the log is either occupied or empty. Empty window = flight. I've added a `slot_frac` column that logs how much non-sky ink sits in that slot every frame — from that, launch and landing times fall out with no new geometry.

    which would have silently broken any launch/flight measurement.

| Path | When | Area |
|---|---|---|

**Resolution: native, no downscale.** 1920×1080 screen (Windows scaling 125 %), grab comes back 1080p pixels, ROI comes back 402×584 pixels. Nothing is resized anywhere.

260: def refine_circle(full: np.ndarray, cx: float, cy: float, r0: float,
261:                   n_rays: int = 720):
262:     """Sharpen a rough (centre, radius) against the actual target edge.
263: 
264:     Hough reported r=106.9 for a target it had measured at r=124.5 a minute
265:     earlier -- 15% off. Every annulus in this program is a multiple of R, so a
266:     15% radius error drags the occupancy scan down into the wood and every
267:     angle then reads 'knife'.
268: 
269:     Rays leave the centre and stop at the first sky pixel. Rays crossing a
270:     protruding knife travel further, so the MEDIAN is the rim. The edge points
271:     are then fed to a least-squares circle fit, which corrects the centre as
272:     well as the radius.
273:     """
274:     h, w = full.shape[:2]
275:     b = full[:, :, 0].astype(np.int16)
276:     rc = full[:, :, 2].astype(np.int16)
277:     sky = (b > rc + 25) & (b > 90)
278: 
279:     lo = int(max(4, r0 * 0.55))
280:     hi = int(min(min(w, h) * 0.5, r0 * 1.70))
281:     if hi <= lo:
282:         return float(cx), float(cy), float(r0)
283: 
284:     pts, radii = [], []
285:     for k in range(n_rays):
286:         a = k * (2.0 * math.pi / n_rays)
287:         ca, sa = math.cos(a), math.sin(a)
288:         for d in range(lo, hi):
289:             px, py = int(cx + d * ca), int(cy + d * sa)
290:             if px < 1 or py < 1 or px >= w - 1 or py >= h - 1:
291:                 break
292:             if sky[py, px]:
293:                 radii.append(d)
294:                 pts.append((px, py))
295:                 break
296:     if len(radii) < 120:
297:         return float(cx), float(cy), float(r0)
298: 
299:     rr = float(np.median(radii))
300:     keep = [p for p, d in zip(pts, radii) if abs(d - rr) < 0.10 * rr]
301:     if len(keep) >= 60:
302:         P = np.asarray(keep, dtype=np.float64)
303:         A = np.c_[2.0 * P[:, 0], 2.0 * P[:, 1], np.ones(len(P))]
304:         rhs = (P ** 2).sum(axis=1)
305:         try:
306:             sol, *_ = np.linalg.lstsq(A, rhs, rcond=None)
307:             cx2, cy2 = float(sol[0]), float(sol[1])
308:             r2 = math.sqrt(max(1.0, sol[2] + cx2 ** 2 + cy2 ** 2))
309:             if (abs(cx2 - cx) < 0.15 * r0 and abs(cy2 - cy) < 0.15 * r0
310:                     and 0.80 * rr < r2 < 1.25 * rr):
311:                 return cx2, cy2, r2
312:         except Exception:                                      # noqa: BLE001
313:             pass
314:     return float(cx), float(cy), rr
315: 
316: 
317: def sky_annulus_frac(full: np.ndarray, cx: float, cy: float,
318:                      r: float, n: int = 180) -> float:
319:     """Fraction of the ring just outside a candidate that is sky-coloured.
320: 
321:     This is the guard against false positives. HoughCircles will happily
322:     invent a circle on a screenshot of an editor -- it found one at (145, 219)
323:     r=90 with 0.7% sky on screen. A real target floats on open sky, so the
324:     annulus around it reads blue. Anything else is not the target.
325:     """
326:     ang = np.linspace(0.0, 2.0 * np.pi, n, endpoint=False)
327:     rs = np.array([1.08, 1.18, 1.28, 1.38])
328:     xs = (cx + r * np.outer(rs, np.cos(ang))).astype(np.int32)
329:     ys = (cy + r * np.outer(rs, np.sin(ang))).astype(np.int32)
330:     h, w = full.shape[:2]
331:     ok = (xs >= 0) & (xs < w) & (ys >= 0) & (ys < h)
332:     if ok.sum() == 0:
333:         return 0.0
334:     px = full[ys[ok], xs[ok]]
335:     b = px[:, 0].astype(np.int16)
336:     rc = px[:, 2].astype(np.int16)
337:     return float((((b > rc + 25) & (b > 90))).mean())

```
Vectorized:
```python
    ds = np.arange(lo, hi)
    ang = np.arange(n_rays) * (2*np.pi/n_rays)
    ca, sa = np.cos(ang), np.sin(ang)
    xs = (cx + ds[:, None]*ca[None, :]).astype(np.int32)   # (nd, n_rays)
    ys = (cy + ds[:, None]*sa[None, :]).astype(np.int32)
    inb = (xs >= 1) & (ys >= 1) & (xs < w-1) & (ys < h-1)
    hit = np.zeros(xs.shape, dtype=bool)
    hit[inb] = sky[ys[inb], xs[inb]]
    found = hit.any(axis=0)
    if found.sum() < 120: return cx, cy, r0
    first = hit.argmax(axis=0)          # index of first True (0 if none)
    radii_arr = ds[first]
    radii = radii_arr[found].tolist()
    pts = list(zip(xs[first, found].tolist(), ys[first, found].tolist()))
```
Careful: `int(cx + d*ca)` truncates toward zero; `astype(np.int32)` also truncates toward zero for positive values. For negative values it truncates toward zero too (numpy astype truncates toward zero). Python int() also truncates toward zero. So they match.

## 2. "Why not 50 fps?"

| Box | FPS | Frame time | Ticks |
|---|---|---|---|
| 400×400 | 60.2 | 16.6 ms | 1 |
| 1280×720 | 60.2 | 16.6 ms | 1 |
| Full screen | 30.2 | 33.2 ms | 2 |

The display hands out frames on a **60 Hz tick = 16.67 ms**. You get 16.67 ms frames or 33.3 ms frames. **Nothing in between.** 50 fps means 20 ms, which is not a multiple of 16.67 — so you'd get alternating 16.7 and 33.3 frames, average 50, individual frames either fast or slow.

=== polar() ===
def polar(img: np.ndarray, mx: np.ndarray, my: np.ndarray) -> np.ndarray:
    return cv2.remap(img, mx, my, cv2.INTER_LINEAR,
                     borderMode=cv2.BORDER_REPLICATE)


def polar_to_game(a_deg: float) -> float:
    """Polar convention (+x = 0, clockwise) -> game convention (up = 0, clockwise)."""
    return (a_deg + 90.0) % 360.0


def runs_of(occ: np.ndarray, min_deg: float, max_deg: float):
    n = occ.size
    d = np.diff(np.r_[int(occ[-1]), occ.astype(int), int(occ[0])])
    starts = np.where(d == 1)[0]
    ends = np.where(d == -1)[0]
    step = 360.0 / n
    out = []
def polar_to_game(a_deg: float) -> float:
    """Polar convention (+x = 0, clockwise) -> game convention (up = 0, clockwise)."""
    return (a_deg + 90.0) % 360.0


def runs_of(occ: np.ndarray, min_deg: float, max_deg: float):
    n = occ.size
    d = np.diff(np.r_[int(occ[-1]), occ.astype(int), int(occ[0])])
    starts = np.where(d == 1)[0]
    ends = np.where(d == -1)[0]
    step = 360.0 / n
    out = []
    for s, e in zip(starts, ends):
        w = ((e - s) % n) * step
        if min_deg <= w <= max_deg:
            out.append((s * step, w))
    return out

=== runs_of() ===
def runs_of(occ: np.ndarray, min_deg: float, max_deg: float):
    n = occ.size
    d = np.diff(np.r_[int(occ[-1]), occ.astype(int), int(occ[0])])
    starts = np.where(d == 1)[0]
    ends = np.where(d == -1)[0]
    step = 360.0 / n
    out = []
    for s, e in zip(starts, ends):
        w = ((e - s) % n) * step
        if min_deg <= w <= max_deg:
            out.append((s * step, w))
    return out

import ctypes
from ctypes import wintypes

MOUSEEVENTF_LEFTDOWN = 0x0002
MOUSEEVENTF_LEFTUP = 0x0004

def click_at(x, y):
    ctypes.windll.user32.SetCursorPos(int(x), int(y))
    ctypes.windll.user32.mouse_event(MOUSEEVENTF_LEFTDOWN, 0, 0, 0, 0)
    ctypes.windll.user32.mouse_event(MOUSEEVENTF_LEFTUP, 0, 0, 0, 0)
```

def sleep_until(t):
    while True:
        rem = t - time.perf_counter()
        if rem <= 0: return
        if rem > 0.0015: time.sleep(rem - 0.0012)
```

So the feedback is **binary** — hit or miss, not "you were 12° off". That means we cannot converge by correcting an angle error. We must **measure** the delay and flight time instead. {
  "newString": "def find_go_button(frame, cx, cy, r):\n    \"\"\"Locate the green GO disc that starts a round.\n\n    Found from the pixels rather than from an offset in units of r, because r\n    changes when the window is resized but the UI bar does not scale with it.\n    Returns (x, y) of the disc centre, or None -- and None means we never\n    click, which is the safe failure.\n\n    Filters that matter, each one earned from a real screenshot:\n      * area in [2500, 40000]   -- the disc is ~100x100 px\n      * 0.75 <= w/h <= 1.33     -- rejects the tall sidebar banners\n      * x within 5r of the log  -- rejects the left-hand banners entirely\n      * y below the log         -- the bar is under the target\n    \"\"\"\n    b = frame[:, :, 0].astype(np.int16)\n    g = frame[:, :, 1].astype(np.int16)\n    rr = frame[:, :, 2].astype(np.int16)\n    mask = ((g > b + 45) & (g > rr + 45) & (g > 110)).astype(np.uint8)\n    n, _lab, stats, cent = cv2.connectedComponentsWithStats(mask, 8)\n    best = None\n    for i in range(1, n):\n        x, y, w, h, area = stats[i]\n        if not (2500 <= area <= 40000):\n            continue\n        if not (0.75 <= (w / max(1, h)) <= 1.33):\n            continue\n        xc, yc = cent[i]\n        if abs(xc - cx) > 5.0 * r or yc <= cy:\n            continue\n        if best is None or area > best[0]:\n            best = (area, float(xc), float(yc))\n    return None if best is None else (int(round(best[1])), int(round(best[2])))\n\n\ndef slot_frac(frame, cyl, r, cxl, height, width):\n    y0 = int(cyl + 2.00 * r)",
  "oldString": "def slot_frac(frame, cyl, r, cxl, height, width):",

}

def build_geometry(cx_l: float, cy_l: float, r: float) -> dict:
    """Precompute remap grids once. Rebuild only when the calibration changes."""
    th = np.arange(N_THETA, dtype=np.float32) * (2.0 * math.pi / N_THETA)
    cos_t = np.cos(th)[:, None]
---
def polar_to_game(a_deg: float) -> float:
    """Polar convention (+x = 0, clockwise) -> game convention (up = 0, clockwise)."""
    return (a_deg + 90.0) % 360.0

def runs_of(occ: np.ndarray, min_deg: float, max_deg: float):

    starts = np.where(d == 1)[0]
